visualization.takeaway: Both models can transact. External payments need a recoverable workflow.
visualization.description: Related customer, refund and approval records can commit together in a Postgres transaction. A support-case document groups messages, proposal and review state; a separately stored balance requires an explicit cross-document transaction design. Both database models can transact. MongoDB supports multi-document transactions; Cosmos DB document API batches share a logical partition key. A provider payment sits beyond either database transaction, requiring provider idempotency and a recoverable workflow. The duplicate-request control illustrates looking up a recorded operation rather than starting a new payment.

visualization.takeaway: Progress travels over SSE. Recovery depends on stored run state.
visualization.description: Read the lanes from agent to application to browser. The application checks access and records run state. Approval is a separate authenticated request. The disconnect example assumes that completion was recorded before the SSE connection dropped. Recovery reads the recorded run without blindly repeating the refund. These are illustrative application event names, not LangChain or AppKit API names. LangChain supplies agent events; AppKit also includes an app server and agent hosting, with the agents plugin in beta. Persistence and recovery must be implemented by the application.
